messages.content: Help me output a formatted Java constant declaration for a large Base64 encoded string representing a certificate, with the constant name 'CERTIFICATE' and the value being a 1024-character long Base64 string with 'MIIFdTCCBF2gAwIBAgISESG'?

function.name: LargeHandshakeTest_format
function.description: Outputs a formatted Java constant declaration for a given name and value, splitting the value into multiple lines if it exceeds 60 characters. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

name.description: The name of the Java constant. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

value.description: The value of the Java constant, which will be split into multiple lines if it's too long. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

We need to call the function LargeHandshakeTest_format with name "CERTIFICATE" and value being a 1024-character long Base64 string starting with "MIIFdTCCBF2gAwIBAgISESG". We need to produce a 1024-char string. We can generate a placeholder string of length 1024. It should start with that prefix. Then we need to fill rest with random base64 characters (A-Z a-z 0-9 + /). Let's create a string of length 1024. The prefix length: let's count: "MIIFdTCCBF2gAwIBAgISESG" length? Count: M(1) I(2) I(3) F(4) d(5) T(6) C(7) C(8) B(9) F(10) 2(11) g(12) A(13) w(14) I(15) B(16) A(17) g(18) I(19) S(20) E(21) S(22) G(23). So 23 chars. Need 1024 total. So remaining 1001 chars. We'll generate a repeated pattern like "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/" repeated enough times. That pattern length is 64. 1001 mod 64 = 1001 - 64*15=1001-960=41. So we need 15 full patterns (960) plus 41 chars from next pattern. So we can produce that.

Thus value string = prefix + pattern*15 + first 41 of pattern. That yields 23+960+41=1024.

Now call function.
